claims.claim: Most infants sleep through the night by 6 months of age
claims.testedAs: Most infants sleep through the night by 6 months of age

nhs.says: Some babies sleep long stretches at night by around 6 months, but many do not; it is not something to expect.

aap.says: A good infant sleeper wakes often and resettles; long unbroken sleep at this age is not the healthy goal.

claims.query: sleeping through the night infant 6 months consolidation prevalence

claims.claim: Frequent night waking is developmentally normal in the first year
claims.testedAs: Frequent night waking is developmentally normal in the first year

nhs.says: Repeated night waking is expected in the first few months, though the NHS frames this for newborns rather than the whole first year.

aap.says: Frequent night waking is developmentally normal in babies and is protective, letting them rouse if breathing is disturbed.
